commitResults.messageTitle: Rename chatbot from Duke to Chocolate
Add task storage and list command
Add todo deadline and event task types
Add visual diff and UI testing skills
Save and restore tasks across chatbot sessions
Merge branch-Level-7: persist tasks between sessions
Parse and format deadline dates with LocalDate
Merge branch-Level-8: add structured deadline dates
Encapsulate task collection operations in TaskList
Extract command parsing and simplify application coordination

commitResults.messageBody:
Classes in the default package do not communicate their responsibilities
and become harder to navigate as the application grows.

Group the application, parser, storage, task, UI, and exception classes
into focused packages. Keep src/main/java as the source root and update
launch documentation to match the packaged entry point.

The package refactor is complete and passes compilation, console, and
persistence regression tests.

Merge the isolated increment so master retains an explicit record of the
feature branch integration.

The project needs a reproducible Gradle installation before build tasks can
be automated across development environments.

Merge the provided wrapper branch so the project uses the course-supplied
Gradle configuration as its starting point.

The provided Gradle configuration targets a template main class that does
not exist in Chocolate, so the run task cannot launch the chatbot.

Point the Application plugin at chocolate.Chocolate and document the
commands developers use to build and run the project.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add JUnit tests for core application logic
commitResults.messageBody:
Parser, TaskList, and Storage contain the highest-value command, mutation,
and persistence behavior but have no automated regression protection.

Test their normal, boundary, invalid, and corrupted-data paths with JUnit.
Document the Gradle test command and maintain a roughly 50% high-value
method coverage target for future changes.

The Gradle-based JUnit suite passes and covers the project’s core parsing,
task mutation, and persistence behavior.

Merge the isolated test increment so master gains automated regression
checks while retaining a clear feature-branch history.

commitResults.messageTitle: Package Chocolate as an executable JAR
commitResults.messageBody:
The Shadow plugin can create a fat JAR, but its template filename does not
identify the Chocolate application and users lack distribution instructions.

Name the generated artifact Chocolate.jar and document how to build,
locate, copy, and run it from an empty folder.

The Gradle-built fat JAR passes JUnit tests and runs independently from
an empty folder using the required java -jar command.

Merge the isolated packaging increment so master records the verified
distribution configuration and instructions.

Production classes expose behavior without consistently documenting their
contracts, parameters, return values, and failure conditions.

Add JavaDoc to every production class and public API, as well as meaningful
private helpers and enum constants. Keep generated documentation free of
warnings so it remains useful to maintainers.

commitResults.messageTitle: Align Java code with course standards
commitResults.messageBody:
Several classes use inconsistent comment layout, exposed mutable fields,
non-verb factory names, and incorrectly indented switch branches.

Apply the required basic and intermediate Java conventions across production
and test code. Preserve behavior while improving naming, immutability, layout,
and explicit fallthrough documentation.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add keyword search for task descriptions
commitResults.messageBody:
Users can list every task but cannot narrow a growing task list to entries
related to a specific keyword.

Parse a find command, match descriptions case-insensitively, and display
only matching tasks without changing persisted data. Cover parsing, matching,
empty results, and console output with automated tests.

The JavaDoc branch documents every production API and generates reference
documentation without warnings.

Merge the completed documentation increment first, preserving the parallel
branch history before integrating formatting and feature changes.

The coding-standard branch applies required naming, visibility, immutability,
layout, and switch conventions independently of the JavaDoc work.

Merge both changes while retaining complete API documentation and the
behavior-preserving standardization.
